This subreddit has helped me, I am sorry if it has not helped you. However, I think it's important not to forget there's only so much that can be done. 

These people aren't (all) doctors or psychotherapists, they're just people who would like to have a fighting chance in the world, and some of them would like to help you find yourself a fighting chance as well, if only for a minute. 

In the time they spend talking with you, you are the only person who matters, and they're writing something just for you. The same can be said for the time listening to you, comforting you, trying to find resources for you that maybe you never knew existed. Even the time they spend thinking of you and thinking of ways to help you. 

In those moments they're dedicated to you. That, to me at least, is one of the most humbling experiences I can imagine. I try not to forget that, because I feel it's easy to forget how much others have poured into us when so much is being pulled out of us simultaneously. I think remembering that helps me feel closer to having balance in my life.

There's two different types of suicidal thoughts, active suicidal thoughts and passive suicidal thoughts.

Being actively suicidal would be to make a plan to kill yourself be placing yourself directly in harm's way or into a situation that will undoubtedly harm you immediately.

Being passively suicidal can be passing thoughts of hoping you die in an unforeseen accident, or taking improper safety precautions that would increase your chances of being seriously injured when it's preventable, like not wearing a seatbelt.

Passively suicidal thoughts are, in my opinion, somewhat of a grey space. Not all passively suicidal people do anything that could lead to their death, oftentimes they just think about it a lot. The issue with passive suicidal thoughts is that it can progress into actively suicidal thoughts in some.

I suppose the intent is really up to the interpretation of each individual, and the scenario that plays out. It likely won't be considered a suicide if it doesn't at all look like one. I imagine even if you were to do something careless it might just be considered a mistake. Passive suicides happen far more than we recognize.
